title: Stuffed Green Pepper, Puerto Rican Style

content.title: About
content.content: Stuffed green pepper, Puerto Rican style is a classic Caribbean dish featuring a sweet bell pepper baked with a filling of rice, meat (usually beef or pork), tomatoes, spices, and sometimes beans. The result is a fragrant, mildly spicy, and richly flavored entrée typical of Puerto Rican home cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is often prepared for holidays and family celebrations.
Traditional seasoning includes adobo – a blend of garlic, oregano, cumin and dried peppers.
In Puerto Rico, peppers symbolize hospitality and abundance.
A variation called “relleno de pimientos” uses seafood or a vegetarian filling instead of meat.
It is commonly served with a tomato‑herb sauce known as salsa criolla.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: Bell peppers provide vitamin C, vitamin A and vitamin B6, which support immunity and vision.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Rice and beans in the stuffing add fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Protein and iron
items.content: Meat contributes complete protein and iron essential for energy and blood formation.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: The dish contains no added sugars, making it suitable for moderate consumption.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Tomato lycopene and spices such as coriander and cumin have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to cumin, oregano or garlic.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Using prepared sauces or broth can raise the salt level; adjust accordingly.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improperly cooked meat may harbor pathogens; ensure internal temperature reaches at least 71 °C (160 °F).

items.title: Heat level
items.content: Reduce or omit chili peppers for those who are sensitive to spiciness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the stuffed pepper hot, often alongside rice, beans or a fresh salad. It can be eaten directly from the baking dish by cutting the pepper in half, or the filling can be scooped out and used as a separate main. A squeeze of lime and a sprinkle of cilantro enhance the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the dish to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer keeping, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly to 74 °C (165 °F) before serving.
